description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09), as the ruled-out wider half of #1247 (b).

    my $x; $x->method_that_is_not_there();
    perl : one line on stderr, exit 255
    PCL  : a fifteen-frame SBCL backtrace, exit 1

s473f gave a PERL die (p-die -> p-exception / p-die-error) perl's exit status
and perl's one line.  It deliberately did NOT widen that to every condition:
an internal CL error is a PCL BUG and its backtrace is the diagnosis the
sweep's crash triage reads.

But PCL raises a lot of PERL-level errors with a bare `(error ...)` -- "Not a
SCALAR reference", "Can't call method X on unblessed reference", "Can't locate
object method ..." -- and those ARE perl dies: PCL's own `eval` catches them
and sets $@, so the toplevel is stricter than eval, which is an internal
inconsistency.

WHAT THIS TASK IS: (1) census the `(error ...)` / `(warn ...)` sites in
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp and classify each as PERL-LEVEL (a die a program can trap
and perl also raises) or INTERNAL (a PCL bug); (2) route the perl-level ones
through p-die; (3) decide what the hook does for the internal ones -- exit 255
WITH the backtrace is probably right, but it changes what the sweep's crash
rows look like, so measure that before deciding.

Two openers were converted in s473f as part of #1247 (b) because their corpus
row needed it: p-use's and p-do's "Can't locate".  ir-conform 022-refs is the
row this task closes.


=== PROGRESS (s495f, 2026-09-25) -- still OPEN ===
p-method-call's three "Can't call method X on unblessed reference / an undefined value / non-blessed reference" sites are p-die now (task #2051's member), so Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t row 11 -- this task's tripwire -- fired as designed and now asserts perl's 255 for that shape.  The census of the OTHER bare-`error` sites is untouched.
subject: CENSUS + DECISION: the runtime raises many PERL-LEVEL errors with a bare CL `error`, so they keep SBCL's backtrace and exit 1 where perl exits 255
